text:
lia: Heads-up — I put together a short proposal for standardizing runtime metrics (token-level latency breakdowns, per-route KPIs) and how we version the schema to avoid insane cardinality. Posting here for feedback.

lia: TL;DR: introduce a small set of coarse labels (route_group, model_family, schema_v) + 'stage' for token path (network, kv_fetch, kernel_exec, decode). Avoid embedding user route paths, exact model sha, or prompt ids in labels. Emit schema_v label (string) rather than creating many new metric names. :thinking_face:

matt: nice. can you spell out exact labels and an example?

lia: sure — proposal snippet:
```yaml
metric: redwood_runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket
labels:
  schema_v: "2"        # bump when label shape changes
  deployment: "hosted|dedicated|private"
  model_family: "mistral-7b|gptx-4"   # coarse family, not exact revision
  route_group: "chat.v1|embeddings.v1|rerank.v1"  # mapped by gateway
  stage: "network|kv_fetch|kernel_exec|decode"
  bucket: 0.001,0.002,...
```

lia: Additional metrics:
- redwood_runtime_token_kv_hits_total (labels: schema_v, deployment, model_family, route_group)
- redwood_runtime_token_kv_misses_total (same labels)
- redwood_runtime_batch_size_distribution (histogram, labels: schema_v, deployment, route_group)

serena: i'm worried about route_group mapping accuracy. gateway needs a small mapping table to canonicalize paths -> route_group. otherwise people will keep pushing raw routes.

matt: agreed. we should add a simple rule: gateway canonicalizes by first two path segments and strips query params. e.g. /api/chat/completions -> chat.v1; /api/embeds -> embeddings.v1. keep mapping in infra repo so product can tweak.

rahul: what about model variants? customers pin exact model revisions for reproducibility. we should not put revision sha in metrics but we do need to know when a model change causes perf shifts. idea: keep model_family label + model_variant sparse label optional. model_variant should be low-cardinality (quantized|fp16|int8|cpu) not commit sha. track commit sha in logs/traces, not metrics.

lia: exactly. keep metrics cheap. if we need per-revision ops later we can add a separate low-volume 'model_release_event' counter tagged with revision for auditing.

matt: naming/versioning Q: prefer schema_v label or new metric names for breaking changes?

lia: schema_v label win: dashboards can filter and we can emit v1/v2 concurrently for a transition window. also avoids explosion in metric count in exporters. downside: some backends (legacy dogstatsd) don't like high cardinality labels — but we've been moving to prometheus/metrics-pipeline. still let's keep schema_v tiny ("1","2").

serena: can we also add a migration plan in the proposal? e.g.:
1) implement v2 exporter behind feature flag on gateway and runtime
2) emit both v1 and v2 for 14 days
3) update dashboards to default to v2 but allow v1 filter
4) after 30 days retire v1 (or extend)

rahul: OK. we also need guidance for dashboards: per-route KPI should be at route_group resolution and show token p50/p95/p99 for "kernel_exec" stage and end-to-end token p99. aggregate by model_family and deployment.

lia: quick example Grafana query (promql-ish):
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{schema_v="2",stage="kernel_exec",route_group="chat.v1"}[5m])) by (le, model_family))
```

matt: looks good. a couple of implementation details:
- exporter should not allocate label arrays per-request; use interned label ids.
- kernel runtime should emit stage timings as int64 microseconds to reduce float noise, exporter converts to seconds.

serena: about KV cache metrics: we should add a kv_fetch_latency histogram with labels {schema_v, deployment, model_family, route_group, kv_outcome="hit|miss|stale"}. but 'stale' should be rare; ok as label. keep per-key info out.

rahul: also add an op-level counter for 'kv_evicts_total' aggregated by model_family to track cache churn. that helps correlate perf regressions after model size changes.

lia: perf regression detection: propose an automated alert policy: if token kernel_exec p95 for any (route_group, model_family) increases >25% vs 7d baseline and absolute p95 > 50ms => open pager (maybe page SRE). For lower tiers send slack alert only.

matt: who owns dashboard updates? @serena?

serena: I'll take dashboards. I'll need the final label set and sample queries to migrate panels.

lia: i'll open a PR for exporter changes with a feature flag. plan: emit schema_v="2" and new labels, AND continue emitting old metrics for 14 days. i'll link migration checklist in PR.

rahul: please include tests validating cardinality remains bounded: e.g., route_group count < 200, model_family < 50, stage < 6.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: metrics-exporter:feature/metric-schema-v2 -> staging at commit 7a1b2c3 (ETA ~3m)

lia: nice — after staging smoke we can flip gateway mapping for a subset of tenants and watch cardinality in the metrics pipeline.

matt: ACTIONS:
- lia: PR exporter + migration checklist (feature flag)
- serena: update dashboards and create v2 panels
- rahul: add unit tests and cardinality gate in CI
- matt: review and coordinate rollout with infra

lia: thanks all. i'll post the PR link here once ready. :+1:
